# History of `experiments/mjc`

*Auto-generated big-picture history. See [`README.md`](README.md) for current status and [`FILES.md`](FILES.md) for the full file index.*

## Why this substrate exists

`mjc` was founded (2026-07-16, [`ideas/physical_control_substrate.md`](../../ideas/physical_control_substrate.md)) to fill a specific gap between the program's two other controllable-dynamics substrates: RHM/MNIST-reaching gives a known, settable DGP but low physical realism; language gives realism but a DGP you cannot dial. MuJoCo was chosen as the middle rung — continuous, contact-rich, real actuation — on the condition that it be used as **a DGP whose knobs you sweep**, never as an RL-to-SOTA robotics benchmark. That discipline (knob sweep + vanilla baseline, no PPO-maxxing) is the one methodological commitment that survives the entire history below unchanged. The doc pitched five cheapest-first cuts: contact-residual structure, arity, dynamics-shift robustness, partial-obs planning, and — billed as "the single biggest open question of the whole program" — whether *drifting* dynamics forces a forward model to grow new representational directions.

## Act I — foundations, and a hub emerges (Cuts #1–#3)

[`contact_residual/`](contact_residual/README.md) verified the ported a2a claim that residual concentrates at dynamical discontinuities, but sharpened it into something more specific: an onset-aligned analysis showed the residual spikes and decays within ~4 steps even though contact persists for 20+ — it marks the *transition*, not the *state*. That single result forced two methodological fixes (Huber over MSE; contact labeled by presence, not proximity) that shaped every FM trained downstream, and it deliberately routed [`arity_torque/`](arity_torque/README.md)'s arity question through free-flight-only transitions so contact difficulty wouldn't confound it. Arity-torque then delivered one of the cleanest results in the whole line: an arity-2 `f(s,u)` FM hits R²≈0.999 at *any* capacity while arity-1 is flat at ~0 at *every* capacity — no amount of capacity substitutes for the missing command input. That arity-2 idiom became the reusable FM used everywhere after.

[`dynamics_shift/`](dynamics_shift/README.md) (Cut #3) is where the substrate earned its keep: it used MuJoCo's unique affordance of intervening on the transition operator while holding the task fixed, showing a model-based agent recovers from a dynamics shift on ~50 reward-free transitions where a protocol-matched model-free policy needs ~240× more *reward-labeled* data. An internal correction here mattered: an early MF baseline that replanned every step was confounded against MB's open-loop commitment, and rebuilding it fairly surfaced the `replan_every` ablation — the reward-free benefit is gated by how ballistic the control is. The README calls this explicitly "the seed of the whole ballistic arc." Cut #3 became the hub the rest of the interface arc forked from.

## Act II — two negatives close a chapter, and the method changes

[`value_shaping/`](value_shaping/README.md) and [`directed_readapt/`](directed_readapt/README.md) split Cut #3's "value ∩ meta" question along a learning-layer/outer-loop line. Value-shaping established the stationary control (a value signal reallocates FM capacity toward what's reachable, away from a value-irrelevant nonlinear field) — worth noting its substrate itself needed a redesign after a first attempt (linear puck dynamics) turned out to give the FM nothing to reallocate away from. Directed-readapt then asked whether disagreement-driven collection beats undirected collection after a shift, and returned two diagnosed negatives: a global shift gives no scarcity to exploit, and under a *local* shift the ensemble is confidently, blindly wrong in the unvisited patch — disagreement never flags it, so directed collection under-visits exactly where it should over-visit. The README names this the end of a chapter: verifying mechanistic atoms one at a time had hit diminishing returns, and the explicit decision (2026-07-18) was to go **phenomenon-first** — build the real compounding-adaptation phenomenon and back-translate mechanism from what works, rather than pre-verifying components. Every node after this one is downstream of that pivot.

## Act III — the interface arc: afferent, efferent, and the blind grader

[`meta_adapt/`](meta_adapt/README.md) reopened meta-learning non-tautologically across five sub-cuts (#4–#4e) and surfaced a dissociation that recurs for the rest of the arc: a context latent can perfectly decode the task (system-ID R²≈1.0) while being *useless* for adaptation unless the task family actually conflicts (#4b); value-directed identification is a robust negative because the most informative command is just the largest one (#4c); and a reward-driven outer loop both prefers and rediscovers value-relevant capacity allocation, but only pays off in control under capacity competition (#4d/#4e). [`curiosity_control/`](curiosity_control/README.md) named itself the missing *afferent* complement to #4d/#4e's *efferent* re-allocation — where-to-collect rather than what-to-model — and reran the same dissociation (tracks a drifting frontier regardless of value-relevance; only pays off in control on-path), plus a substrate inversion of the active-vision line: pure curiosity here chases aleatoric noise (noisy-TV), fixed not by a smarter filter but by grounding — adding exploit as a second additive drive with an interior optimum.

[`online_value_loop/`](online_value_loop/README.md) tried to fuse both taps into one live loop and found it **obstructed on both levers**: the afferent loop has no gradient because CEM-MPC replanning is nearly blind to the tracking gap, and the efferent loop's benefit is a transient invisible to any converged-competence probe. Rather than a dead end, this was read as confirmation that the two-timescale split is *forced*, and it reframed value's payoff as an *adaptation-speed* effect — naming [`drift_value_loop/`](drift_value_loop/README.md) verbatim. That node found real compounding, but reassigned its source from value-carving (capacity-gated, control-robust) to the fast context-latent memory, and diagnosed the deeper obstruction precisely: reactive control is a near-blind grader of the FM, full stop. Regrading the outer loop on FM prediction error instead of downstream reward gave the explore/exploit balance a clean optimum for the first time — "the missing piece was the teacher, not the value structure."

[`ballistic/`](ballistic/README.md) resolved that "blind grader" finding as a fact about *control mode*, not value: replanning re-grounds every step and absorbs staleness regardless of what the value structure is doing underneath. Switching to feedforward, committed control makes FM quality ~3× more behaviorally load-bearing and reward-free re-adaptation ~4.3× more effective — closing the efferent bridge that had looked inert for two prior nodes. Its own leftover caveat (directed collection confounded by corridor geometry) is what [`ballistic/directed/`](ballistic/directed/README.md) picked up, and what the on-policy line later re-attempted honestly (below).

## Act IV — realism hardening, and two humbling corrections

[`arm_substrate/`](arm_substrate/README.md) (2026-07-22) was built because the pusher's near-linear dynamics required faking capacity competition and locality through six hand-tuned force layers — the arm was meant to get both from physics. Two self-corrections shaped it: capacity only binds intrinsically at n≥5 links (not the "natural" 2-link arm), and several apparent substrate failures at higher link counts turned out to be an under-sized CEM planner silently flattening a 42-dim problem, not a real effect. It explicitly flagged that acquisition was still teleport-based and would inherit the pusher's known subsidy problem unchanged — the direct hinge into [`on_policy/`](on_policy/README.md).

`on_policy/` (2026-07-24) is the line's most important self-correction. Its own headline: what had looked like an "embodiment" advantage in earlier framing was mostly a **mistuned teleport sampling knob** — an oracle teleporter told where to sample closed almost the entire gap, meaning the honest fix was retuning the baseline, not crediting the body. What *is* genuinely structural is command-state entanglement, which quietly exposed Cut #2's i.i.d.-command premise as a teleport-only luxury. A second correction followed immediately: the team's own prior guess that on-policy coverage would smooth a step-like recovery into a gradual one was refuted *backwards* — it's teleport that looks gradual, and that too was the same mistuned knob. Embodiment only costs something real once drift is made spatially local (2.5× more transitions, mechanism: data gathered while the model is wrong is itself wrong-distributed). [`on_policy/directed_on_policy/`](on_policy/directed_on_policy/README.md) then resurrected the retracted directed-collection claim once monitoring was metered against the same budget (1.84× vs. the old 22× subsidy), and it paid off again. [`on_policy/metered_repair/`](on_policy/metered_repair/README.md) (2026-07-30) ported two RHM claims onto this substrate: the diagnosis transfers cleanly, but the *repair* mostly doesn't (1/3 seeds), and a fixed-DOF plant with spatially-gated fields turned out to give the FM no route to shared-parameter inference across regions — a clean negative explained mechanistically rather than left as noise.

## Act V — closing the founding question, and retiring part of the founding frame

[`expansion/`](expansion/README.md) (2026-07-27) finally ran Cut #5, the "single biggest open question" from the founding doc, after three earlier rank-based instruments had failed from readout saturation and forced a three-piece calibrate→measure→calibrate design. The result: drifting a fixed-DOF plant's physics does **not** open the forward model's representational frontier (±0.08 directions) against a genuine support-increase calibration of +0.72±0.42 on the same instrument — roughly 10× smaller. This directly confirmed [`beliefs/dimensionality_expansion.md`](../../beliefs/dimensionality_expansion.md) §Scope, added days earlier, which had argued a motor plant has no hierarchy to expand into and should show a flat frontier as *health*, not failure. The founding idea doc's claim that "drifting dynamics is a novelty generator" is now explicitly marked retired — drift still matters for realism and for the whole value-loop arc's non-stationarity, but it no longer has special standing with respect to representational growth. The belief's actual core claim (does novelty grow representable directions at all?) is noted as still untested anywhere; that question was handed off to RHM, the one substrate in the program with real hierarchical structure.

## Throughline

Read end to end, the arc's real subject is not any single result but a recurring self-diagnosis: nearly every "surprising negative" (directed collection missing confident-wrong regions, curiosity chasing noisy-TV, control being a blind grader of value, on-policy's advantage being a mistuned baseline) was eventually traced to a *measurement or protocol artifact* rather than a fact about the world, and fixing the instrument — not abandoning the hypothesis — is what usually unlocked the next positive result. The other constant is disciplined narrowing: five founding cuts became a much deeper, forked arc precisely because early negatives (directed_readapt, online_value_loop) were treated as informative pivots rather than dead ends, and the one closed door (expansion) was closed with a calibrated null, not an absence of result.
